summary: Go SDK retry middleware regenerates opaque session id on retry, causing duplicate remote tool/function invocations
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external tool (webhook) invocations when the Go client retries a streaming request. The customer is using a custom retry middleware that injects an opaque session identifier into X-Redwood-Idempotency for each attempt.

Impact:
- Duplicate side effects observed in downstream systems (two webhook posts for same logical tool execution).
- Customer is seeing increased billing for duplicated work and inconsistent application state.
- Reproducible for a subset of requests that hit a proxy chain (edge sidecar -> CDN) before reaching Redwood API.

Environment:
- LiteraHealth dedicated account on us-west-2, Go SDK v0.9.7 with in-house retry middleware.
- Requests are long-running streaming with function/tool calls (external webhook triggered by function tool).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a streaming session from the Go client that triggers a function/tool call (webhook) from the model.
2) Simulate transient network failure between client and edge sidecar to cause client retry.
3) Observe that retry middleware generates a new X-Redwood-Idempotency value on the retry attempt.
4) Server processes both attempts as distinct and executes the tool/webhook twice.

Observed behavior:
- Two webhook POSTs within ~2s for the same user action.
- Server logs show two different idempotency header values for the two attempts.
- Edge proxy logs indicate header truncation to 32 bytes for the regenerated value.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should preserve the idempotency key for the logical request so downstream function/tool calls are deduplicated by the server.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- Client header on initial attempt: X-Redwood-Idempotency: "sess:QmFzZTY0VXNlcjoxMjM0NTY="
- Client header on retry attempt: X-Redwood-Idempotency: "sess:QmFzZTY0VXNlcjoxMjM0NTYgLTAtcmVuZ2Vu"
- Edge proxy truncation observed: header passed to api-gateway: "sess:QmFzZTY0VXNlcjoxMjM0NTYgLT"
- Server treated truncated header as a different idempotency key and executed tool twice.

Customer-provided notes:
- "We intentionally re-generate a session-level nonce when retrying to separate retransmits, but assumed the server would canonicalize by prefix. We didn't expect the sidecar to clip the value and cause a collision."

investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- Reproduced duplication locally using customer's retry middleware.
- Root cause chain: (1) middleware regenerates an opaque idempotency value containing base64 + metadata; (2) intermediate edge proxies truncate header to 32 bytes; (3) server treats truncated string as distinct key -> duplicate execution.
- Edge sidecar previously enforced strict header size for custom headers to prevent large header abuse; default was 32 bytes.
- Two mitigations validated: a) server-side canonicalization that extracts 'sess:' prefix and base64-decodes/pads before dedupe (requires careful compatibility); b) client-side best practice to preserve idempotency across retry attempts or emit a short stable token.
- Related to earlier ticket SUP-980999 (mux-reconnect out-of-order tool ack and orphaned effects) which also discussed header normalization.
resolution:
Partial/temporary resolution applied 2026-03-13:
- SRE relaxed header size limit for X-Redwood-Idempotency on a test subset of edge sidecars to 128 bytes to reduce truncation risk (edge-sidecar-#3124).
- Provided customer with recommended client change: preserve the original X-Redwood-Idempotency value across retry attempts in their middleware. Shared code snippet and suggested unit tests.
Planned permanent fix:
- Implement server-side canonicalization and normalization for idempotency header parsing to tolerate common encodings and trailing truncation patterns. This will be gated and feature-flagged; GH PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789.
- Add SDK-level helpers and a retry-preserve option in Go SDK v0.9.8 to make correct behavior the default for customers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412.
Follow-ups:
- QA to run focused e2e with common proxies and CDNs to ensure no other headers hit similar truncation problems.
- Security review on relaxing header limits to ensure no request-splitting or header-bloat attack surface introduced.
